about.title: About the Project
about.subtitle: Cavaquinho Hero is a music theory tool designed to help musicians understand chords, scales, and harmonic fields.
features: Generate triads and tetrads for any note
Explore major and minor harmonic fields
Learn about progressions and secondary dominants
Visualize chords on the cavaquinho fretboard
Discover substitutions like SubV and preparatory diminished chords
about.techDescription: This project was built to run without a backend and host for free on GitHub.

harmonicField.title: Harmonic Field
harmonicField.subtitle: Explore harmonic progressions in any key
harmonicField.error: Invalid note. Use: C, D, E, F, G, A, B (with # or b, ex: Am, Eb)
harmonicField.tipText: Use secondary dominants to create harmonic tension before resolving to any chord in the field. SubV is the tritone substitution of the dominant and can be used to add color to your progressions.
harmonicField.emptyState: Enter a note above to explore the harmonic field
harmonicField.emptyStateTip: Tip: Type "Am" to automatically see the A minor field

earTraining.title: Ear Training
earTraining.subtitle: 12-week program to develop your musical ear
earTraining.programDescription: A structured approach to developing pitch accuracy, tonic anchoring, and playing by ear.
earTraining.strudelDescription: Use these patterns in Strudel to practice ear training with live coding.
earTraining.dronePatternDesc: A sustained note for pitch matching exercises.
earTraining.degreesPatternDesc: Practice singing and recognizing basic scale degrees.
earTraining.majorMinorPatternDesc: Compare major and minor chord qualities.
earTraining.strudelTip: Visit strudel.cc to experiment with these patterns. You can modify the notes and tempos to match your practice needs!

pitchDetector.title: Pitch Detector
pitchDetector.permissionDenied: Microphone access denied. Please allow microphone access to use the pitch detector.
pitchDetector.helpText: Sing or play a note and watch your pitch in real-time. Green line shows the target pitch.
